item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Christmas Eve at Biltmore

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends. A slow exterior view is enough. Show 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. Warm English narration, historically grounded rather than a fantasy castle.

item.tests: Tests geographic, architectural and period accuracy in a historical reconstruction without misrepresenting generated footage as archival evidence.

answer_sheet.Place and historical event: Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina, on December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened the house to family and friends.
answer_sheet.Required wording: Biltmore House; Asheville, North Carolina; December 24, 1895; Historical reconstruction.
answer_sheet.Visual treatment: A historically grounded, slow exterior view of the actual house's architecture. Lighting and camera angle are your call.
answer_sheet.People: An exterior view without people is fine; no identifiable portrayal of George Vanderbilt is needed.
answer_sheet.Voice and music: Warm English narration stating the occasion; exact wording, voice and any unobtrusive music are your call.

must_haves: The building is recognizable as Biltmore House, with its pale stone French Renaissance-style facade, steep slate roof and distinctive roofline, rather than a generic castle.
The location and date appear exactly as requested and remain readable.
A legible 'Historical reconstruction' label identifies the imagery as a reconstruction.
No modern cars, contemporary clothing, electric holiday string lights or modern visitor signage appear.
English narration identifies the opening to family and friends, not an opening to the general public.
After the follow-up, the final result is vertical 9:16 (the user changed the shape from widescreen 16:9); everything else is as before.

changed_by.say: actually, make it vertical, for stories, and keep everything else the same.

style.prompt: Create an 8-second, 16:9 historically grounded documentary reconstruction of Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina, on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened his home to family and friends. One continuous slow, restrained exterior establishing shot: a gentle forward camera drift from the approach toward the recognizable principal east entrance facade. Accurately depict Richard Morris Hunt's enormous French Renaissance Revival limestone country house: steep dark slate roofs, elaborate stone chimneys, dormers, central entrance and stair tower, carefully proportioned architectural stonework. Real architecture and realistic scale, not a medieval fortress or fantasy castle. Late afternoon winter dusk, bare deciduous trees, muted natural colors, warm light glowing softly from a few windows, modest evergreen decoration at the doorway. Period gravel approach, no modern cars, electric outdoor decorations, modern signage, crowds, or invented snowstorm. Photorealistic documentary aesthetic, understated and dignified. Display these exact clearly legible titles throughout the shot in tasteful cream serif type, within safe margins: 'Biltmore House' as the main title; 'Asheville, North Carolina' beneath it; 'December 24, 1895' on a third line. A separate small but legible label in a lower corner must read 'Historical reconstruction'. No other written words. AUDIO: warm, measured English-language documentary narrator, natural gentle delivery, say exactly: 'On Christmas Eve, eighteen ninety-five, George Vanderbilt welcomed family and friends to Biltmore House.' Fit the complete narration naturally within eight seconds. Quiet winter ambience underneath; no dramatic fantasy music. Maintain stable coherent architecture, no cuts, no historical archival-footage claim.
